speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for coming in. You mentioned experiencing occasional shooting ear pain and difficulty wearing earrings after your tympanoplasty; to better understand what is happening, could you describe exactly where the pain is located and what triggers it?

speaker: Patient
text: 25-year-old female. The patient has a history of polycystic ovarian syndrome, depression, and chronic bilateral ear infections. She underwent right ear tympanoplasty 12 weeks ago. Although audiology report from one week ago showed improved hearing by 20 decibels, she reports occasional shooting pain when eating and discomfort when wearing earrings. She describes her job as stressful and mentions poor sleep quality.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Chronic Otitis Media with Granuloma (Post-Tympanoplasty).

The patient's history of recurrent bilateral ear infections, combined with the new onset of shooting pain during chewing (suggesting referred otalgia or trismus) and intolerance to earrings (suggesting a posterior canal mass), strongly points to a granuloma or granulation tissue at the tympanic ring or canal wall, which can occur months after surgery.

I will proceed with a physical exam and imaging to confirm.
